clue.text: Accommodated — may be taken aback!'

indicators.note: taken aback suggests reading the letters backwards, and here they come out the same either way

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A host exclaims that a guest given lodging may be startled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken aback' looks like surprise, but it means read backwards: the answer is the same in both directions.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone up is to give them lodging, so accommodated is the past tense of that phrasal verb.

clue.text: Drips toiling hard?

parts.note: someone working hard gives off drops of sweat, so the whole clue describes sweating

explanation.surface: Feeble people are seen working strenuously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drips' looks like a noun for wimps, but it is a verb: what a hard worker's skin does.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweating from exertion is what a hard-toiling body does, dripping moisture through the skin.

clue.text: Food for a tot's mashed up

indicators.note: mashing breaks things up and rearranges them, so the letters of these words are shuffled

explanation.surface: Baby food for a toddler has been mashed.
explanation.definitionFit: Grilled bread is an everyday food, eaten at breakfast.

clue.text: Bothersome, but turning out about all right

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a thing proving true is turning out to be true
OK means all right

explanation.surface: Something annoying ends up being fine after all.
explanation.definitionFit: Something irritating or annoying is provoking: it stirs up vexation.

clue.text: The plant getting a loan isn't going broke

indicators.note: broke suggests something smashed into pieces, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A plant borrows money from someone who is not facing bankruptcy.
explanation.definitionFit: Santolina is a genus of aromatic shrubs, also called cotton lavender.

clue.text: A dotty way to do the decorating!

definitions.text: A dotty way to do the decorating!

parts.words: A dotty way to do the decorating!
parts.note: dotty seems to mean crazy but here means made of dots, a paint technique

explanation.surface: Someone takes an eccentric approach to painting the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dotty' suggests mad, but it literally means applied in dots.
explanation.definitionFit: Applying paint in small dabs or dots to create texture is a decorating technique.

clue.text: Pay no attention to scamp

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to scamp work is to do it carelessly and skimp on it

explanation.surface: Ignore the young rascal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignoring something is failing to care for it, and scamping a job means skimping on it carelessly.

clue.text: Eliminated friction with drunk

definitions.meaning: slang for intoxicated, well lubricated with alcohol

explanation.surface: Someone smoothed over a quarrel with a drinking companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Lubricating machinery removes friction, and well lubricated is slang for tipsy.

clue.text: An isolated community lives without scandal

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: he lives means he is, he exists
slander is scandalous talk

explanation.surface: A remote community lives free of gossip.
explanation.definitionFit: People living on a remote offshore isle form a cut-off community.

clue.text: Set beside a light

parts.note: a beam is a ray of light

explanation.surface: A lamp is placed next to something.
explanation.definitionFit: A nautical term for lying at right angles to a ship's keel, alongside it.

clue.text: Thought to phone about one point a boy made

indicators.note: about means going around, so the phone word encloses the rest

parts.note: to ring is to phone
E is one point of the compass, east
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: Someone thinks of phoning about a point a lad made.
explanation.definitionFit: Logical thinking or argument, the process of working something out in the mind.

clue.text: A story absorbing novices in the city

indicators.note: absorbing means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a lie is a story, a fib
L stands for learner, so two learners are LL

explanation.surface: A tale draws in beginners living in town.
explanation.definitionFit: A large city in northern France, capital of the Nord region.

clue.text: The courtyard is quiet at ten

parts.note: P is piano, quiet in music
IO looks like the figures 1 and 0, so ten

explanation.surface: The yard is peaceful at ten o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: A paved outdoor area beside a house, originally an inner courtyard in Spanish homes.

clue.text: Putting up moneys, possibly around five hundred, in an assumed name

indicators.note: around means the shuffled letters surround another piece
possibly signals that the letters could form something else when shuffled

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

explanation.surface: Someone puts up cash, perhaps about five hundred, under a false name.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen name or alias adopted in place of one's real one.

clue.text: Serving men set about the little page slacking off

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, men serving in the army

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the placing word goes around the page

parts.note: to site something is to set or place it
P is the short form of page

explanation.surface: Soldiers arrange things around a lazy young page-boy.
explanation.walkthrough: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a British Army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: A respite is a break or pause, a period of easing up from effort.

clue.text: To-do about a travel-bag needed for the flight

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the commotion word goes around the A

parts.note: a stir is a commotion, a to-do
a case is a suitcase for travelling

explanation.surface: A fuss over a suitcase needed for an air journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' suggests a plane trip, but it is a flight of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight of steps is a set of stairs between floors.

clue.text: Assayers of British coinage at one time

definitions.meaning: the tester was an old English silver coin, later a slang name for a sixpence

explanation.surface: Analysts examine old British coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Assayers check samples, and the tester was a Tudor shilling, later sixpence, in old British money.

clue.text: Not readily giving credit

parts.note: giving credit looks like a lender's business, but here it means believing

explanation.surface: A lender is slow to extend loans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Credit' suggests banking, but to give credit is to believe.
explanation.definitionFit: A doubter is slow to believe claims, being inclined to doubt.

clue.text: Wouldn't compete, yet scored

explanation.surface: A competitor didn't take part, and yet won points.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse withdrawn from a race is pulled out, and a scored surface bears cut marks.

clue.text: Heartless fool with aim to acquire a decoration

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter is removed

parts.note: a sap is a fool
to angle for something is to aim at it

explanation.surface: A heartless idiot schemes to get a medal.
explanation.definitionFit: A sequin, a small shiny disc sewn on clothes for ornament.

clue.text: "What can — sots, or slaves, or cowards?" (Pope)

definitions.text: "What can — sots, or slaves, or cowards?" (Pope)

parts.words: "What can — sots, or slaves, or cowards?" (Pope)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Alexander Pope's Essay on Man, the missing verb meaning to dignify

explanation.surface: A line of verse asks what could dignify drunkards, slaves or cowards.
explanation.walkthrough: The couplet ends 'Alas! not all the blood of all the Howards', the Howards being a noble English family.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise to the nobility or dignify, the verb Pope's line needs.

clue.text: A writer, given direction, writes letters for the queen

parts.note: S is south, a compass direction
pens means writes
ER, Elizabeth Regina, are the letters for the queen

explanation.surface: An author, told which way to go, composes letters to the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Edmund Spenser wrote The Faerie Queene, so the queen fits the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: An Elizabethan poet, author of The Faerie Queene.

clue.text: Upsetting clients? Cut it out!

indicators.note: upsetting means knocking over, so these letters are tipped into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone told to stop annoying the customers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut it out!' sounds like 'stop that', but it literally describes how the answer is made.
explanation.definitionFit: A template made by cutting a pattern out of a sheet, then painted through.

clue.text: Fish with an engineer maybe

parts.note: a perch is a freshwater fish
CE is a civil engineer

explanation.surface: Perhaps one fishes with an engineer.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned word for perhaps or possibly.

clue.text: Push into a cupboard

definitions.meaning: a cupboard, especially one built into a wall, in Scottish and Irish use

explanation.surface: Shove something into a cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: To press is to push, and a press is an old word for a linen cupboard.

clue.text: The ad that's dubious is disliked

indicators.note: dubious means questionable or not right, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A misleading advert is unpopular.
explanation.definitionFit: Something loathed or detested is strongly disliked.

clue.text: It's dogma — note catch

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale
to net is to catch

explanation.surface: Some doctrine is told to note and grab hold.
explanation.definitionFit: A principle or belief held as true, a doctrine.

clue.text: Her upbringing causes one sorrow

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing up means reading the letters from bottom to top

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
to moan is to express sorrow

explanation.surface: A woman's childhood upbringing makes someone sad.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Bible Naomi, bereaved, asked to be called Mara, meaning bitter.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name, borne by Ruth's mother-in-law in the Old Testament.

clue.text: Orderly out of work

parts.note: ex means out of or former
an act is a deed or piece of work

explanation.surface: A hospital attendant is out of a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orderly' looks like a hospital worker, but it is the adjective meaning precise.
explanation.definitionFit: Precise and methodical, a meaning shared by neat and tidy.

clue.text: Support church people appearing on the stage

parts.note: to back is to support
the cloth means the clergy

explanation.surface: Churchgoers back a performance in the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A painted curtain hung at the rear of a theatre's scenery.

clue.text: Veronica's career flourishing

parts.note: to career is to rush along, to speed
doing well means flourishing

explanation.surface: A woman named Veronica has a thriving career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Veronica' looks like a woman's name; it is a plant genus.
explanation.definitionFit: The plant genus Veronica has small blue flowers, commonly known by this name.

clue.text: Scottish bigwig disposed to receive Russian leader

indicators.note: to receive means to take in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: laid means set out or disposed

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A Scots landowner is minded to welcome a head of Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish landed proprietor, the lord of an estate.
